fatal_errors: No prior evidence is cited or identified, despite the explicit requirement to support the mechanistic premise.

The cast-versus-HEBM/SPS comparison simultaneously changes grain size, phase fractions, dislocation density, porosity, and processing history, so it cannot distinguish their individual mechanistic contributions.
explanation: The hypothesis closely reconstructs the target material, HEBM/SPS intervention, processing window, nanocrystalline 83% FCC/17% BCC mediator, Hall–Petch/dislocation/solid-solution strengthening interpretation, and predicted hardness and compressive strength. It also captures the room-temperature compression scope, limited ductility, and processing boundaries. Its main weakness is evidence discipline: the supporting-evidence fields are empty and no specific prior observations are identified. The proposed experiment verifies the overall processing–structure–property association but is not a well-controlled mechanistic test because casting and HEBM/SPS differ in several coupled variables. A stronger design would include SPS-only and milling-duration or annealing controls, measure density and dislocation density, and test whether strength tracks grain size after porosity and phase fraction are held constant. The falsification rule also overcommits to the exact 83/17 phase ratio, even though the core strengthening hypothesis could remain valid at a different phase ratio.
